To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. The sum-energy spectra for the production of positron electron pairs in heavy-ion collisions are not consistent with a single power law over the entire measured range, but rather are better represented by the sum of a power law and an exponential.

(a) no statistically convincing evidence for sharp structures in the sum-energy spectra for pairs of positrons and electrons is observed in our data; (b) the production rate for positron-electrons in our data is in good agreement with the rate predicted by the statistical model of the hot nucleus; and (c) the data are not inconsistent with the hypothesis that the positron-electron pair yield is proportional to the number of neutrons in the hot nucleus.

(i) The APEX spectrometers are capable of detecting and analyzing positron-electron (e{sup +}-e{sup -}) pairs produced in collisions of heavy ions, with a sensitivity that is comparable to that of the best spectrometers used for this purpose in the 1970s and 1980s.
